chunks: Every action should be a named command in one registry so keys and the palette can find it. Start with new-tab and close-tab; the split work adds its commands here.
Keybindings should only name command ids, never call layout code. That keeps the registry the one entry point.

search_doc.semantic_identifier: [SPL-102] Split a pane vertically or horizontally
search_doc.blurb: Add split-vertical and split-horizontal commands with default keys (ctrl+shift+d, ctrl+shift+e). The new pane takes focus and the width is shared evenly.

chunks: Add split-vertical and split-horizontal commands with default keys (ctrl+shift+d, ctrl+shift+e). The new pane takes focus and the width is shared evenly.
Even split for now; resizing comes in its own issue.

search_doc.blurb: A toggle-orientation command (ctrl+shift+o) flips the split between vertical and horizontal.

chunks: A toggle-orientation command (ctrl+shift+o) flips the split between vertical and horizontal.
Decision: toggling orientation keeps the focused pane first, so the cursor never jumps. We considered swapping the pane order and rejected it.
Implemented as setOrientation in SplitPane.ts; it writes the orientation into PaneLayout.
Checked after SPL-104 merged: a toggled tab comes back toggled when you switch back to it.

search_doc.semantic_identifier: [SPL-104] Restore pane layout when switching tabs
search_doc.blurb: Switching away from a tab and back should bring back its orientation, panes and focus. The tab manager reads the pane layout state when it restores a tab.

chunks: Switching away from a tab and back should bring back its orientation, panes and focus. The tab manager reads the pane layout state when it restores a tab.
Restoring a tab brings back orientation and focus; pane sizes reset to an even split for now.
Note this depends on the orientation work in SPL-103: a toggled tab must come back toggled.

search_doc.blurb: resize-pane-left and resize-pane-right (ctrl+alt+left, ctrl+alt+right) move the focused pane's border by the paneResizeStep setting.

chunks: resize-pane-left and resize-pane-right (ctrl+alt+left, ctrl+alt+right) move the focused pane's border by the paneResizeStep setting.
Decision: the minimum pane width is 10 columns, so two panes fit in an 80-column terminal with room for borders.
Resize step defaults to 2 columns (paneResizeStep in the settings file).
Decision (replaces the 10-column minimum above): the minimum pane width is 20 columns. Ten columns truncated every prompt in user testing.

search_doc.blurb: Should the resize step be configurable?

chunks: Should the resize step be configurable? Two columns per keypress feels right on a laptop.
Agreed. Put it in the settings file as paneResizeStep so people can change it without a release.
